standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness of presentation over a scheme theoretically dense open, openness of a flat and locally finitely presented morphism, and dimension zero fibres

standard_prerequisites.name: Scheme theoretic density under flat base change, descent of finiteness, and finite flat morphisms being finite locally free
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms, labels morphisms-lemma-flat-morphism-scheme-theoretically-dense-open (proof line 3110), morphisms-lemma-finite-flat (proof line 3118) and morphisms-lemma-finite-locally-free (proof line 3121); Descent, label descent-lemma-descending-property-finite (proof line 3116)
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows the inverse image of the dense open remains scheme theoretically dense so that the empty part W must vanish, lets finiteness descend back to the base, and upgrades finite flat to finite locally free so that the degree can be compared over the dense open.

core_obligations: Normalise the situation: the morphism is locally of finite presentation by the dense open lemma, its image is open so the base may be replaced by that image, then the base may be taken affine and the source quasi-compact by working with quasi-compact opens with full image, so that the morphism is separated, quasi-compact, flat and locally of finite presentation (proof lines 3083-3092).

Show the fibres are finite: all fibres have dimension zero by the dimension over a dense open lemma, hence the morphism is quasi-finite, and at a point s of the base one chooses an elementary etale neighbourhood g : (T, t) -> (S, s) such that the base change splits as V disjoint union W with V -> T finite and the fibre of W over t empty (proof lines 3093-3101).

Eliminate the empty part: since the base changed morphism is flat and locally of finite presentation its image of V is open in T, so after shrinking T one has T = pi(V); as f is an isomorphism over U the base changed morphism is an isomorphism over the inverse image of the dense open, hence that inverse image lies in V, and by flatness it is still scheme theoretically dense in the whole base change, which forces W to be empty; therefore the base change is finite over T (proof lines 3102-3112).

Conclude: finiteness descends to an open neighbourhood of s in the base, a finite flat morphism is finite locally free so after shrinking the morphism has some degree d, and d equals one because the degree is one over the scheme theoretically dense open U; hence the morphism is an isomorphism, and since s was arbitrary the original morphism is an open immersion (proof lines 3113-3123).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a quasi-compact separated flat morphism onto its image over an affine base (proof lines 3083-3092).
Use dimension zero fibres and the etale splitting of the quasi-finite part (proof lines 3093-3101).
Use scheme theoretic density over the dense open to kill the empty part and make the base change finite (proof lines 3102-3112).
Descend finiteness, compare degrees over the dense open and conclude an isomorphism (proof lines 3113-3123).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is a Zariski main theorem style criterion: a separated flat locally finite type morphism which is an isomorphism over a retrocompact scheme theoretically dense open is itself an open immersion (statement lines 3072-3081, tag 081M). The proof does real work at each step: it upgrades local finite type to local finite presentation over the dense open, reduces to a quasi-compact flat morphism onto its image over an affine base, uses dimension zero fibres and the etale splitting of the quasi-finite part to write the base change as a finite piece plus a piece empty over the closed fibre, and then kills that second piece by scheme theoretic density, before descending finiteness and comparing the degree with one over the dense open. The density argument is the substance, so the claim is H2.
